question: How and where was each tissue grown and sampled (germination conditions and age for GRoot/GShoot, leaf-3 stage, field site and year for adult leaf and kernels)?
proposed_answer: Fill growth_system, stage and age from the Methods of Kremling et al. 2018 (Nature 555:520, doi:10.1038/nature25966); until then NR.
evidence: The Nature article is behind a login and has no PMC copy. Open papers on the same data give only the tissue definitions (Giri et al. 2021, doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1009568; Li et al. 2018, doi:10.1101/gr.229716.117); Blanc et al. 2021 (doi:10.1093/g3journal/jkab004) says 'grown in a common garden'. BioSample SAMN06764809: post-flowering leaf, kernels 350 GDD after pollination, geo_loc_name USA.

question: What do the 8 and 26 in LMAD8/LMAD26/LMAN8/LMAN26 mean, and how should they enter the analysis?
proposed_answer: Two sampling dates (or plantings) matched to flowering time. Keep them in sampling_group, compare day with night within line and group, and never use the group as a factor on its own: it is confounded with germplasm.
evidence: Line sets are disjoint between groups except B73 and W22R-rstd. Group 8: 140 genotypes, 5 tropical; group 26: 125 genotypes, 50 tropical. Within a group almost every line has both day and night (80 of 81 day lines in group 8, 124 of 124 in group 26).

question: Are a line's LMAD and LMAN libraries paired (same plants or plot), so night vs day can be a paired contrast?
proposed_answer: Yes: fit night vs day paired by line within sampling group (DESeq2 ~ genotype + time), as MaizExpressC does for its diversity panel. Whether it is the same plant or the same plot does not change the fit.
evidence: 203 genotypes have both LMAD and LMAN libraries, almost always in the same sampling group.

question: What are the 11 libraries labelled LMid (10 genotypes, 2 of them B73)?
proposed_answer: Leaf 3 middle from a pilot set: quantify them, confirm by expression after library QC (they should sit between L3Base and L3Tip), and use them only alongside the pilot's own L3Base libraries, not pooled with the 26 L3Mid libraries.
evidence: All 11 are in submission 10344823 (flowcell HHT7JBGXX). Seven of the genotypes plus B73 also have an extra L3Base library in pilot submission 10344825 (flowcell HHV55BGXX, 28 libraries in all). The BioSample lists leaf 3 middle as the only middle-leaf tissue. L3Mid (26 libraries) are all on plate KAKRNA28.

question: Use the 26 L3Mid libraries (26 lines, each also with L3Base and L3Tip), which Lei et al. 2025 left out?
proposed_answer: Yes, as the middle point of the leaf-3 gradient (base, middle, tip) for those 26 lines; leave them out of tissue-wide statistics that rely on ~250 lines.
evidence: Li et al. 2018 used them for the base-to-tip gradient (their Fig. 4B, 26 samples).

question: Can the 12 landraces in the library names (MR01-MR21, 29 libraries) be matched to Lei's 14 BKN011-BKN035 lines?
proposed_answer: Keep them under their library names (genotype_class landrace, subpopulation NR, no Lei link) unless a key turns up, e.g. the taxa names in Kremling's processed expression files on CyVerse (HapMap 3.2.1 names).
evidence: Three MR lines are named after landraces (MR02_Assiniboine, MR19_Santo_Domingo, MR20_Shoepeg). Lei Table S1 gives only origin for the BKN lines. The CyVerse files could not be fetched by script (redirect to its unblock page).

question: Accept the name matches that are not exact (metadata/build/line_aliases.tsv)?
proposed_answer: Accept Il101T = Il101, Il677a = i1677a (typo in Lei), Yu796NS = Yu796, and the spellings Ill_Hy/IllHy and MS71/Ms71. KUI2021 = Ki2021 is probable: confirm.
evidence: Each Lei name has exactly one candidate in the library names; KUI2021 is a Thai tropical line name variant not seen elsewhere.

question: What is B73-10 (7 GShoot libraries, plate KAKRNA14, flowcell HLN37BGXX)?
proposed_answer: A B73 seed lot or a check set. Use the libraries as B73 batch controls in library QC; keep them out of line-level statistics.
evidence: Only the label; no other tissue has B73-10.

question: B73Htrhm (6 libraries) and W22R-rstd (5) are not in Lei's Table S1: keep them?
proposed_answer: Keep them as other inbreds with subpopulation NR; they get no eQTL or TWAS links.
evidence: B73Htrhm is a B73-background disease-resistance stock; W22R-rstd is the W22 R-r:standard color stock.

question: How should the 111 B73 libraries (all tissues, 20 of 23 flowcells) be used?
proposed_answer: As batch controls in library QC (plate and flowcell effects) and as the reference line in the app, shown as the mean of its libraries per tissue.
evidence: B73: L3Base 27, L3Tip 26, GRoot 17, LMAN 14, Kern 11, GShoot 8, LMAD 6, LMid 2.

question: 34 non-B73 genotype x tissue pairs have two libraries (Kern 13, L3Base 12, L3Tip 4, GShoot 2, GRoot 1, LMAD 1, LMAN 1): keep both?
proposed_answer: Keep both through QC; per-line values are the mean of the libraries that pass. Seven of the L3Base pairs are the pilot set (see LMid).
evidence: metadata/samples.tsv, replicate column.

question: Which trimming and quantification settings for these 3' libraries (single-end 85-90 nt, NextSeq 500, poly(T)-primed)?
proposed_answer: At M2, look at the first reads of a few runs (poly-A, adapters, fixed bases at the 5' end) before fixing the trimming, then quantify without length correction as for the 3' tag study in MaizExpressC (Xue2021).
evidence: Li et al. 2018: poly(T)-primed 3' mRNA-seq, 4-15% of reads from 45S rRNA. The library kit is not named in any open source.

question: Where should the FASTQ (532 GB) and the results go on Hazel?
proposed_answer: As for N and C: FASTQ, work, containers and logs under /share/maize/rrellan/MaizExpressD; gene tables and MultiQC in /rsstu/users/r/rrellan/sara/MaizeExpressD/results/Kremling2018 (Mac: /Volumes/rsstu/users/r/rrellan/sara/MaizeExpressD). Reuse the B73 v5 salmon index from MaizExpressN.
evidence: ENA fastq_bytes total 532 GB, 1,960 files.

question: Which tissue contrasts should M4 test (metadata/contrasts.tsv, 12 drafted)?
proposed_answer: The four from HANDOFF.md, each for the panel and for B73: leaf maturation L3Tip vs L3Base (plus L3Mid vs L3Base and L3Tip vs L3Mid for the 26 lines with all three positions, panel only), day/night LMAN vs LMAD, adult vs seedling leaf LMAD vs L3Tip, organ GShoot vs GRoot. Sign: log2(numerator / denominator), stated in sign_note.
evidence: python3 -I metadata/build/validate_contrasts.py: 0 problems. Line pairs with a library passing QC on both sides: L3Tip vs L3Base 243, LMAN vs LMAD 185, LMAD vs L3Tip 180, GShoot vs GRoot 217, L3Mid vs L3Base 24, L3Tip vs L3Mid 25. B73 libraries after QC: L3Tip/L3Base 25/22, LMAN/LMAD 6/6, LMAD/L3Tip 6/25, GShoot/GRoot 8/17. Not in any contrast: all 254 Kern libraries (no developmental partner), LMid (display only), B73-10, the pilot L3Base libraries, and libraries of lines missing the partner tissue (e.g. 59 LMAN libraries of lines without a day library in their group, plus B73's 7 group-8 night libraries); all of them still enter per-tissue expression and tissue specificity.

question: How should the panel contrasts be fitted?
proposed_answer: DESeq2 ~ pair + tissue on the libraries passing QC of lines with both tissues (pair = line; line and sampling group for day/night), as MaizExpressC's Zhou2022 panel; B73 and B73-10 left out of the panel. Repeat libraries of a line enter as extra libraries of its pair. Counts without length offsets (3' tags); ashr-shrunk log2FC for display; MaizExpressC's single_library rule.
evidence: Most lines have one library per tissue, so the pairing by line removes genotype from the tissue effect. B73 has 6-25 libraries per tissue and would weigh like 6-23 one-library lines if left in, so it gets its own contrasts instead. The largest fit has 262 pairs (about 525 libraries and 263 coefficients); if DESeq2 is too slow on the Mac it runs on Hazel, with the same model.

question: Keep separate B73-only contrasts (replicated, ~ 0 + tissue) for the reference line?
proposed_answer: Yes: they give the B73 response with real replicates, for the app's reference line and to compare with the panel. B73-10 stays out (M1).
evidence: B73 day/night uses sampling group 26 only (B73 by day was sampled only there). B73 L3Base excludes the 2 pilot libraries.

question: Fit day/night with both sampling groups together (paired within line and group), and each group alone as a secondary check?
proposed_answer: Yes. Groups are not a factor of their own (M1); the two per-group contrasts are tagged secondary.
evidence: Group 8: 70 line pairs after QC, group 26: 115; only W22R-rstd (and B73) were sampled in both. B73 LMAN libraries agree at r 0.94-0.96 within a group and 0.87 across groups (M3), so the group matters and pairs never cross it.

question: Most contrasts compare libraries sequenced on different flowcells (tagged flowcell_confounded): accept without a flowcell term?
proposed_answer: Yes, and note it in Methods. A flowcell term cannot be estimated (each flowcell holds mostly one tissue), and the B73 controls show flowcell effects are small.
evidence: Line pairs sharing a flowcell: day/night 2 of 185, the other panel contrasts fewer than 10%; the L3Mid contrasts are all on one flowcell (HJ7FKBGXX). B73 libraries of one tissue agree at r 0.94-0.97 on the same flowcell and 0.94-0.96 across flowcells, against 0.80-0.85 between different lines on one flowcell (genes >= 20 CPM).

question: LMAD vs L3Tip compares field adult leaf by day with seedling leaf 3: keep it, tagged conditions_differ?
proposed_answer: Yes, with the caveat in its notes and in the app: stage and sampling date differ, and growth conditions may too.
evidence: Seedling leaf 3 and adult leaf after flowering were sampled at different stages and dates; how each was grown is still NR in samples.tsv (item growth_conditions).

question: How should per-line and per-tissue expression be summarised for the app?
proposed_answer: Per line and tissue: mean CPM (and TPM) of its libraries passing QC (M1: mean of repeat libraries); B73 as the mean of its libraries. Per tissue: median and interquartile range over lines. All 9 tissues, LMid included (display only).
evidence: Salmon quantified these 3' tags without length correction (M2).

question: Which tissue-specificity measures?
proposed_answer: Both, on the seven tissues of Lei et al. 2025 (L3Mid and LMid shown but not scored): (1) Lei's method: per gene, scaled log2 counts regressed on tissue vs the rest (t statistic), top 5% per tissue and median fold change >= 2 against every other tissue; (2) tau (Yanai et al. 2005) on the per-tissue medians of line means, log2(CPM + 1), tissue-specific when tau >= 0.8.
evidence: Lei found 37-317 tissue-specific genes per tissue (median 185) on B73 v3. The two lists will be compared once Lei's table is on v5 gene IDs (M5).

question: How should variation among lines be measured?
proposed_answer: Per tissue and expressed gene (median CPM >= 5): the variance of log2 CPM among lines (one library per line), and the share of it beyond the variance among B73 libraries of that tissue (plant, batch and depth noise): (V_lines - V_B73) / V_lines, set to 0 when negative. Shown in the app with the per-line values.
evidence: In M3 the variance among B73 libraries was 2.6-5.4 times what read sampling alone predicts, and 27-59% of the variance among lines (median over genes, by tissue), so subtracting it matters.
